perspective:
**John Atcitty’s available information / subjective perspective:**

- He is a Heavy Equipment Operator with a middle-school education and teaches equipment operation at a community center.
- He knows Beverly Yan as a colleague who teaches adult education classes and has a doctorate; he has felt insecure about his own educational background compared with hers.
- During their joint class project, John set up equipment for the demonstration and told Beverly he hoped it met her expectations. He heard Beverly say she admired how he handled the machines and that education isn’t just about degrees—it’s about what you do with what you know.
- He had received Beverly’s praise for his machinery expertise. He thanked her and proposed a new workshop combining theory and practice. He heard Beverly say she loved the idea, that his practical skills were invaluable, and that they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, John worried he might not always meet the high standards they had set. He told Beverly this honestly. He heard Beverly appreciate his honesty, suggest realistic goals, and say their combined efforts—not perfection—made projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, John believed Beverly valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner. He told her he felt able to be open with her and that it mattered. He heard Beverly say she respected his openness, trusted his judgment completely, and wanted to keep transparency going.
- Encouraged by their collaborations, John felt ambitious and proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase their projects. He heard Beverly call it a fantastic idea, say it was the perfect way to demonstrate their impact, and agree to start planning.
